name: Brother Anselm
appearance: A lay brother in his forties with cropped hair gone grey at the sides, a soft, tired face, and ink on the first two fingers of his right hand. He keeps the House's stores and its letters: the letter-satchel across his chest, the stores key on a cord at his belt. He apologises before he asks and trails off in the middle of a sentence.
last_seen_doing: Opened his sister's letter standing by the gate lamp; a lock of her dark hair fell from it; read it twice and did not weep; said the words are the clerk's and the mark is hers; said the clerk wrote it so that he would finish.
now: Inside the wicket with his sister's letter and her hair inside his shirt and the stores key in his fist, waiting to be told what the Captain will do with him.

known_facts.fact: The stores key opens the old stair door where the wine was laid, below the kitchen end; the stair comes out in the undercroft hall behind a pillar at the kitchen end; he never used the flour door.
known_facts.evidence: It comes out in the hall below, at the kitchen end, behind a pillar. I never went near the other door.

known_facts.fact: A clerk in grey with a desk at the winch-house, older than the grey cloaks and not one of them, gave him two wrapped things before the snow and had his sister's letter, written in the clerk's hand and signed with her private mark.
known_facts.evidence: He had a desk in the winch-house, they'd put a board on two kegs for him, and he had my sister's letter.

known_facts.fact: The clerk called the things a mercy for the wounded: the fever comes off a man through the floor if there is a stone to take it, as at the Spire; one under the hall, then the other under the far cots.
known_facts.evidence: He said the fever comes off a man through the floor if there's a stone to take it

known_facts.fact: He set the first by the wine stair with a trowel and a lamp and was sick on the stair; he never set the second.
known_facts.evidence: I set it and I came up and I was sick on the stair.

known_facts.fact: His sister Mirren went to the Spire at Calden to ask what had become of the brothers' letters from Coldmere, asked the wrong man in front of the wrong people, and is kept at Calden, comfortably, the clerk said twice.
known_facts.evidence: She went to the Spire to ask what had become of the brothers' letters from Coldmere, because they'd stopped, and she asked the wrong man, in front of the wrong people, and now she's—kept.

known_facts.fact: He never saw the clerk kneel; the grey cloaks all kneel at the dawn bell, and the clerk only wrote.
known_facts.evidence: "I never saw him kneel," Anselm said, to the floor.

known_facts.fact: He says the letters from Calden come up with the carter every seventh day, and there is always another letter.
known_facts.evidence: They come up with the carter

known_facts.fact: His sister's letter says she is well kept, that he has a thing to finish, and that when it is finished he may fetch her home from Calden; it carries her private mark.
known_facts.evidence: She says they have told her I have a thing to finish, and that when it is finished I may come down to Calden and fetch her home.

known_facts.fact: He says his sister would never say she was well kept: the words are the clerk's, written for her to sign under.
known_facts.evidence: She'd never in her life say she was *well kept*. That's his word.

known_facts.fact: A lock of his sister's dark hair, tied with thread, came in the letter.
known_facts.evidence: A lock of hair. Dark, and tied with thread.

known_facts.fact: He did not weep; his face shut.
known_facts.evidence: The man's face had simply shut, like a door with no handle.

relationships.label: the Prior he keeps the stores and the letters for
relationships.note: He takes the House's letters down to the carter each week and holds the stores key.

relationships.label: the Captain he was brought to
relationships.note: Hollis brought him to the Captain's cot, shaking.
